LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest players in NBA history. He was born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, and played high school basketball at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he gained national attention as a prodigy. After being selected first overall in the 2003 NBA Draft by the Cleveland Cavaliers, LeBron quickly became a dominant force in the league.

He has won four NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) with three different teams—Cleveland Cavaliers, Miami Heat, and Los Angeles Lakers—and earned four NBA Most Valuable Player awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013). LeBron is known for his versatility, combining scoring, passing, rebounding, and defensive prowess. Off the court, he is also recognized for his philanthropy, notably through the LeBron James Family Foundation, which focuses on education initiatives such as the I PROMISE School in Akron.
